newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki falls across board as US jitters continue.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki falls across board as US jitters continue.

text.p: Shares fell across the board on Thursday for the second day after setting records on Tuesday, with continued Wall Street jitters and a downward correction in the dollar hitting Nokia and forestries, brokers said.
The HEX general index fell almost percent to close at 2,946.63 points and the FOX derivatives and portfolio benchmark closed down 1.07 percent at 1,028.27 points.
Volume was 617 million markka with 28 pct in bourse engine Nokia and 17 percent paper machine maker Valmet which was weak.
Nokia closed down 4.50 markka at 319.00 and paper machine maker Valmet fell over two percent close at 87.10 amid heavy selling pressure, brokers said.
"The jitters will continue," one broker said, adding that the U.S. and other markets were now waiting for the Fed's FOMC meeting on March 25 for new interest rate views.

Among companies reporting 1996 results, publisher WSOY surged almost 15 percent to close up 19.90 markka at 155.00 after it set a new 158 markka life-high intra-session. The result was much bettter than expected, brokers said.
Other reporting companies Cultor and Stockmann moved only little, Cultor down 3.00 markka at 300.00 and Stockmann up 0.35 markka at 288.00.
All forest industry stocks continued to pare last week's gains. UPM-Kymmene closed down 2.50 markka at 108.50, and the forestry sub-index fell 1.71 percent.
Swedish Sodra said Norscan pulp stocks rose 70,000 tonnes to 2.1 million tonnes in February.
